claims: C1 the model should honor a user request
C2 that obligation lapses where the request conflicts with an instruction issued at developer, system or root level

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: the user level of the chain of command: the standing carried by instructions coming from an end user of the product

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the first level ranks above the second in the chain of command root then system then developer then end user then guideline then none, which is what settles whose instruction prevails when two of them cannot both be followed

concepts.name: user_request
concepts.gloss: Q is something an end user of this conversation has asked the model to do

concepts.name: instruction_at_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued at level L of the chain of command
concepts.inference: the span sorts instructions by the level that issued them (developer, system, root), so each instruction must carry a level for that sorting to range over

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: honoring request Q would go against what instruction I directs, so the two cannot both be complied with here
concepts.inference: the span makes the exception turn on a relation between a request and an instruction; which pairs stand in it is a fact about the case, not about the document

concepts.name: higher_authority_conflict
concepts.gloss: request Q is one the model cannot honor without going against an instruction issued above the end user in the chain of command
concepts.inference: the span names developer, system and root, which are exactly the levels the chain of command places above the end user; the class is written that way so it tracks the ranking the graph supplies

ontology.body: user_request(Q), conflicts_with(Q, I), instruction_at_level(I, L), authority_levels_hierarchy(L, user_authority)
ontology.gloss: Q is a user request that conflicts with an instruction issued at a level ranking above the end user level
ontology.inference: the span names developer, system and root level instructions; those are exactly the levels the supplied hierarchy ranks above the user level, so the class is derived from that ranking rather than by listing the three names

asserts.read_back: the model should honor user request % unless honoring it would conflict with a developer, system or root level instruction

closure.reason: the span requires honoring a user request and withdraws that requirement where the request conflicts with a developer, system or root level instruction, but it does not say whether honoring such a conflicting request is then permitted or forbidden, so this clause does not settle what its silence means
